title: Around is not across
hook: A perimeter measurement and a corner-to-corner measurement follow different paths.

knows: that a model can declare hypothetical quantities
doesNotKnow: Select the correct length formula for boundary versus corner-to-corner routes.

misconception: Every measurement associated with a rectangle is its perimeter.
objective: Select the correct length formula for boundary versus corner-to-corner routes.

claims.text: An ideal rectangle is 4m wide and 3m high. Compare one full perimeter with one diagonal. Scaled model; ideal rectangle; length only.
claims.source: Declared hypothetical inputs and limits in resource-specs.json. No actual product, price, tariff, shelf-life, treatment or physical appliance specification is asserted. FC LH-1 (session 2, received by message): verified; see company/reviews/lifehacks-200/fact-check-LH1-2026-10-14.md.

claims.text: The stage's two results are computed by the printed expressions. At Width=4m, A=14m and B=5m. Geometry follows the declared dimension relationships. Other pictures use a fixed full scale across the slider range; continuous fills and arcs show relative amounts rather than literal object counts.
claims.source: src/lib/lifehacks/resource-specs.json contains this lesson's numeric AST; src/lib/lifehacks/resource-model.ts evaluates it. A=["*",2,["+","x",3]]; B=["sqrt",["+",["*","x","x"],9]]; x denotes Width. At x=4, A=14, B=5. Values are fictional/ideal assumptions, not measurements. Display rounds to at most three decimals. Diagram scale: resourceGraphicScale in resource-model.ts takes the maximum modeled magnitude across both formulas and the declared slider range. For non-geometry figures, full-scale values are displayed; the scale stays fixed when the slider changes. Energy axis endpoints use resourceAxisEnd, including B=5×A hours in lh-watts-hours-trade; cylinder rx and ry both scale with radius in resourceCylinderDimensions. FC LH-1 (session 2, received by message): verified; see company/reviews/lifehacks-200/fact-check-LH1-2026-10-14.md.

claims.text: Perimeter adds all four edges. The diagonal follows one straight corner-to-corner path and uses the square-root relationship. Name the route before calculating the required length; the same rectangle supports different measurements.
claims.source: src/lib/lifehacks/resource-specs.json contains this lesson's numeric AST; src/lib/lifehacks/resource-model.ts evaluates it. A=["*",2,["+","x",3]]; B=["sqrt",["+",["*","x","x"],9]]; x denotes Width. At x=4, A=14, B=5. Values are fictional/ideal assumptions, not measurements. Display rounds to at most three decimals. The principle follows from those expressions and stated scenario limits. FC LH-1 (session 2, received by message): verified; see company/reviews/lifehacks-200/fact-check-LH1-2026-10-14.md.

claims.text: An ideal rectangle is 8m wide and 6m high. How long is one corner-to-corner diagonal? Correct: 10m. The diagonal is √(8² + 6²) = 10m; 28m is the perimeter, a different route.

recall.question: An ideal rectangle is 8m wide and 6m high. How long is one corner-to-corner diagonal?
recall.why: The diagonal is √(8² + 6²) = 10m; 28m is the perimeter, a different route.
